Cycling in Seattle

Rail-trail to the lake, ferry to the island, STP in July

Getting around. The rules.

Seattle is a city you ride out of on trails and ferries. The Burke-Gilman runs from Shilshole Bay past the University of Washington to Bothell, almost all of it off the road. The Lake Washington loop is 50 miles around the lake. The Bainbridge ferry leaves Colman Dock downtown, and the Chilly Hilly course starts at the other end. Cascade Bicycle Club leads free group rides most days of the week, and its Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic leaves the University of Washington on July 10, 2027. Delta, Southwest and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026). Link light rail takes you and the bike from the airport to downtown in 38 minutes.

Best months
July, the driest month: an average high near 77°F and less than an inch of rain (WeatherSpark). The Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic leaves the University of Washington the second weekend of July. Cascade Bicycle Club's free group rides go out all year, and the club requires full fenders on its rides when the roads are wet. Its season opens on Bainbridge Island with Chilly Hilly in February; the event page says to wear layers and be ready for rain.
Nearest airport
Seattle-Tacoma International (SEA), 14 mi

Clubs and collectives in Seattle

  1. Cascade Bicycle Club

    The region's big club and the STP's organizer. Its volunteer-led free group rides go out most days of the week from Seattle and the Eastside, posted about a week ahead on the club's ride calendar: MUMPS (Mondays, 10:00 am), TREATS (Tuesdays, 10:00 am), LUMPS (Wednesdays, 11:30 am), ROAD (Wednesdays, 6:00 pm), Eastside Tours (Thursdays, 6:20 pm), the Issaquah Social (Thursdays, 11:00 am), FRUMPS (Fridays, 10:00 am) and Eastside Hills (Saturdays, 10:00 am). Free, but register for each ride on the site, wear a helmet and be there for the safety briefing; each pace, from Steady (12–14 mph) up, is its own group.

  2. Outspoken Cycle Club (Seattle)

    LGBTQ+Beginner friendly

    Seattle's queer and allied cycle club, in its own words. Social rides run from beginner-friendly outings to day-long rides around the region, plus trips to rides elsewhere. Every ride is posted and signed up for on its Heylo page: in 2026 that meant spring and summer weeknight rides (Mercer Mondays from the East Portal Viewpoint, a no-drop West Seattle Wednesday ride from the Seacrest water taxi dock) and, this October, a three-ride chocolate-stop series. Join the Heylo group and pick a ride.

  3. NorthStar Cycling Club

    BIPOCNo-drop

    A Central District club whose aim, in its own intro, is to "Get Melanated People on Bicycles." Sunday Service (Sundays, 10:30 am) leaves the clubhouse at 21st and Union: easy pace, no-drop, all levels invited, with a few bikes to rent. Fill in the club's waiver before you ride; the Wednesday Mercer Island ride is on hold.

    In the directory: NorthStar Cycling Sunday Service (Sundays, 10:30 am) →

  4. Moxie Monday

    Women / trans / femmeNo-drop

    A monthly evening ride "for folks who are femme, trans, non-binary, gender non-conforming, and/or women," on any kind of bike, from Westlake Park downtown. Easy pace, 8 to 15 miles; the group stays together and picks the route before it rolls. Show up; ice or snow cancels. Instagram @moxiemonday.

    In the directory: Moxie Monday (1st Monday of the month, 6:00 pm) →

  5. Good Weather

    No-drop

    The Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) leaves Tailwind Cafe, 1424 11th Ave, on Capitol Hill: in the group's words, "our weekly no-drop ride around town," with park sits and pastry stops at 10 to 12 mph. It also posts faster rides and the odd campout. Show up.

    In the directory: Good Weather Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) →

How Seattle rides: the zones, getting here

About Seattle

The riding leaves the city four ways. North and east on the trails: the Burke-Gilman from Shilshole Bay through Fremont and the University District to Bothell, then the Sammamish River Trail to Redmond. Around Lake Washington: the 50-mile loop, Mercer Island across the I-90 bridge, Seward Park on the Seattle shore. Into the Eastside hills: Zoo Hill on Cougar Mountain above Bellevue, the Issaquah trails, the Snoqualmie Valley Trail's gravel out of Carnation. And onto the water: Alki and the West Seattle loop, the Elliott Bay Trail from the Olympic Sculpture Park, and Bainbridge Island by ferry from Colman Dock. The neighborhoods a visitor sleeps in are the University District (the STP start), Capitol Hill, downtown and the Chinatown–International District; Fremont and Ballard have the trail and the beer garden but no hotel this guide could find. Every listing says which part of town it sits in.

The Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic, 206 miles to Portland in one day or two, has started here since Cascade Bicycle Club established it in 1979. The 2027 ride leaves the University of Washington's E-18 lot at 5 a.m. on Saturday, July 10, and Robert is riding it. The club's other big days start in or near town too: Chilly Hilly on Bainbridge Island in February, the Emerald City Ride in spring and RSVP, Seattle to Vancouver, in August; Obliteride rides out of Seattle the same month. The dates are in the 2027 list on this page. If you are here for the STP, the Burke-Gilman runs past the start on campus, and the rest of this guide is what to do with the days before and after.

Riding in Seattle

The ride for the evening you land is the Burke-Gilman. It's a rail-trail from Golden Gardens past the Ballard Locks, Gas Works Park and the University of Washington to Bothell, about 19 miles one way. Turn around whenever you want. The long one is the Lake Washington loop, 50 miles and about 1,900 feet, counter-clockwise from South Bellevue; join it at Seward Park if you're staying in the city. The short lake ride is Mercer Island, 17 miles across the I-90 bridge with one real climb. The climb is Zoo Hill on Cougar Mountain, a 9-mile loop from Lewis Creek Park at 8 to 13 percent most of the way. The gravel is the Snoqualmie Valley Trail from Carnation, 38 miles, half of it on the trail. The ferry day is Bainbridge Island: roll on at Colman Dock and ride the 33-mile Chilly Hilly course. The north end of the lake is an almost-all-trail loop of 35 miles from Log Boom Park in Kenmore, and West Seattle is a 12-mile loop from Seacrest Pier past Lincoln Park and Alki. The trails are shared with everyone on foot, and Cascade's lake-loop page says Seattle's roads are in poor shape; the route pages carry the rest.

The group rides are the way in, and most of them are Cascade Bicycle Club's: free, posted about a week ahead, register on the site, helmet on, be there for the briefing. LUMPS (Wednesdays, 11:30 am) leaves Matthews Beach Park on the Burke-Gilman for a pie stop in Bothell; MUMPS (Mondays, 10:00 am) leaves Log Boom Park in Kenmore for loops of the lake's north end and Mercer Island; TREATS (Tuesdays, 10:00 am) goes out from the Eastside, often to the Snoqualmie Valley; FRUMPS (Fridays, 10:00 am) moves its start each week. The hill ride is Eastside Hills (Saturdays, 10:00 am) from the Kirkland Transit Center, 50 to 60 miles in pace groups; the winter night ride is ROAD (Wednesdays, 6:00 pm) out of Redmond, lights required; Eastside Tours (Thursdays, 6:20 pm) and the Issaquah Social (Thursdays, 11:00 am) are the Thursdays. Off the club calendar: Good Weather's Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) rolls from Tailwind Cafe on Capitol Hill, no-drop, at 10 to 12 mph; NorthStar Cycling Club's Sunday Service (Sundays, 10:30 am) leaves its Central District clubhouse, no-drop, all levels; Moxie Monday (1st Monday of the month, 6:00 pm) is the monthly ride for femme, trans, non-binary and women riders from Westlake Park; Mello Fellos' Saturday ride (Saturdays, 8:00 am) leaves the downtown shop; Critical Mass (Last Friday of the month, 6:30 pm) gathers at Westlake Park. Outspoken Cycle Club, Seattle's queer and allied club, posts its rides on Heylo.

The 8 routes, with maps →

Getting to Seattle

Fly into Seattle-Tacoma International (SEA), about 14 miles south of downtown. Link light rail leaves from the airport garage: trains every 8 to 10 minutes most of the day, 38 minutes to downtown, and on to the University of Washington; bikes roll on free. You don't need a car. The Burke-Gilman, the West Seattle loop and the Bainbridge ferry start in the city, the north-lake loop can start at UW Station, and the lake loop passes Seward Park. Only Zoo Hill and the Carnation gravel loop want a car or a long ride out. Coming home from Portland after the STP, Amtrak Cascades has ten $5 bike racks on every train (Oct 2026), or Cascade's own buses bring riders and bikes back to UW. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the ferry fare, each transit agency's bike rules and the shops that rent.

Questions about riding in Seattle

Should I bring my bike to Seattle?

Yes, for three days or more. Delta, Southwest and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026). No Seattle shop says on its site that it receives a shipped bike, so flying it is the way. Renting wins only on a one- or two-day trip: Métier on Capitol Hill rents a Cervélo or a Tarmac SL8 at $125 to $175 a day and evo in Fremont a carbon road bike at $100 (Oct 2026). For the STP's 206 miles, ride your own.

Do I need a car to ride in Seattle?

No. The Burke-Gilman, the West Seattle loop and the Bainbridge ferry start in the city, the north-lake trail loop can start at UW Station on Link, and the Lake Washington loop passes Seward Park. Link light rail carries bikes free from the airport, King County Metro buses have a three-bike rack, and Washington State Ferries board bikes first. Only Zoo Hill, from a Bellevue park, and the Carnation gravel loop want a car or a long ride out.

Can I take my bike on the ferry to Bainbridge Island?

Yes. Roll onto the Bainbridge ferry at Colman Dock on the downtown waterfront: $11.35 for an adult plus a $1 bicycle surcharge, paid at Seattle only, nothing to pay coming back (fares for Oct 4, 2026). Be there 20 minutes early; bikes load onto the forward end of the car deck and unload ahead of the cars; you can leave the bike there during the crossing, take your bags, and don't get off without it. The Chilly Hilly course, 33 miles and about 2,150 feet, starts at the other end, and Pegasus Coffee House is the coffee off the boat.

Where do group rides start in Seattle?

Most are Cascade Bicycle Club's free rides, posted a week ahead on its calendar: LUMPS (Wednesdays, 11:30 am) from Matthews Beach Park on the Burke-Gilman, MUMPS (Mondays, 10:00 am) from Log Boom Park in Kenmore, Eastside Hills (Saturdays, 10:00 am) from the Kirkland Transit Center, ROAD (Wednesdays, 6:00 pm) from Redmond in winter. Good Weather's Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) leaves Tailwind Cafe on Capitol Hill; NorthStar's Sunday Service (Sundays, 10:30 am) leaves the clubhouse at 21st and Union; Moxie Monday (1st Monday of the month, 6:00 pm) and Critical Mass (Last Friday of the month, 6:30 pm) gather at Westlake Park; Mello Fellos' Saturday ride (Saturdays, 8:00 am) leaves the shop downtown. Outspoken Cycle Club, the queer and allied club, posts its rides on Heylo.

Can I rent a road or gravel bike in Seattle?

Yes. Métier Cycling & Café on Capitol Hill rents a Cervélo Caledonia or Soloist at $125 a day and a Specialized Tarmac SL8 or Cervélo Aspero gravel bike at $175, with the pedals you ask for, closed Mondays (Oct 2026). evo in Fremont rents a carbon road bike at $100 a day or $500 a week, no model named (Oct 2026). Mello Fellos downtown rents road and gravel bikes without a published price. For Tiger Mountain's trails, Ride Bicycles in Issaquah rents mountain and e-mountain bikes. Nobody lists sizes; call with your height.

How do I get back to Seattle after the STP?

Two ways from Portland, both with the bike. Amtrak Cascades has ten bike racks in the baggage car on every train, $5 each, booked as a bicycle space with your ticket; they sell out in summer, so book early (Oct 2026). Or Cascade's own buses: in 2026 Bus & Bike was $115 and Bike-Only $70 by July 5, loading at the Portland finish Saturday night, Sunday afternoon and Monday morning, with bikes back at UW that Sunday or Monday. Watch the 2027 transportation page when registration opens in January.
